core: Unsupervised learning as machine learning that finds patterns in data without pre-existing answers or labels
Clustering as the main idea: grouping similar items together
Other unsupervised tasks: anomaly detection (finding unusual items) and dimensionality reduction (reducing many features to fewer)
The one-sentence distinction from supervised learning: labels vs. no labels
Where unsupervised learning appears: customer segmentation, recommendation systems, organizing documents
The caveat: patterns found may or may not be meaningful; human judgment decides
supporting: Association rule mining as a further unsupervised task ('frequently bought together' patterns)
Unlabeled data as the input to unsupervised learning
Anomaly detection's use in fraud detection

Machine learning fundamentals and model training (sibling topic machine-learning-basics owns them)

claims.claim: Unsupervised learning is a type of machine learning that analyzes unlabeled data and discovers patterns on its own, without pre-existing answers or human-provided labels.

The main difference between supervised and unsupervised learning is the type of input data: supervised learning relies on labeled training data with known correct answers, while unsupervised learning works with unlabeled data.
Clustering is the most popular unsupervised learning approach; it breaks raw, unlabeled data into groups of similar items based on their similarities and differences.
Unsupervised learning is commonly used for customer segmentation, grouping customers by common traits or purchasing behavior to guide marketing and business strategy.
Anomaly detection is an unsupervised learning application that discovers data points that are atypical or unusual within a dataset, which can reveal fraud or other abnormal behavior.

Dimensionality reduction is an unsupervised technique that reduces the number of features, or dimensions, in a dataset, making large datasets easier to work with and visualize while preserving essential information.
Unsupervised learning is used to organize documents and news articles into categories when no category labels exist.
An unsupervised algorithm groups data but does not itself understand what the groups mean; people interpret the groupings and judge whether the patterns are meaningful and useful.
Association rule mining is an unsupervised task that finds items frequently purchased or occurring together, powering 'frequently bought together' style recommendations.

conflictingEvidence.issue: How many main unsupervised task types there are: Google Cloud and IBM both enumerate three (clustering, association, dimensionality reduction), while many introductions present clustering alone as the core idea.
positions: Google Cloud and IBM describe clustering, association rules, and dimensionality reduction as the three main unsupervised learning tasks
Introductory treatments often foreground clustering as the defining unsupervised idea
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson presents clustering as the main idea, names anomaly detection and dimensionality reduction as other tasks, and mentions association only briefly, which is consistent with both framings and with the no-math literacy level.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Whether anomaly detection is a distinct unsupervised task type or an application of clustering.
positions: Google Cloud lists anomaly detection among real-world examples of unsupervised learning
IBM's learning-methods index treats anomaly detection as its own unsupervised learning method
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson names anomaly detection as an unsupervised task without endorsing a strict taxonomy, so either framing supports the statement.
